title: Outlook: custom organisation properties on profile cards
summary: The briefing passes: the planned capability, January rollout targets and admin-required default match Microsoft's records. The control routes and Graph calls are documented, and the page distinguishes general connector licensing and existing Entra controls from the new properties.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans organisation-specific custom properties on Microsoft 365 profile cards.
claims.quote: Customers can now customize their M365 profile cards by adding custom properties unique to their organization.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance guidance; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Admins can add up to 10 custom properties.
claims.quote: You can add up to 10 custom properties to profile cards using Microsoft Graph People connectors.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The properties can come from external systems such as HR platforms.
claims.quote: These properties can be sourced from external systems like HR platforms, enriching user profiles with relevant organizational details.

claims.claim: Admins can configure a display name for each property.
claims.quote: Admins can configure visibility, display name, and icon for each property in Microsoft 365 admin center

claims.claim: Admins can configure an icon for each property.
claims.quote: Admins can configure visibility, display name, and icon for each property in Microsoft 365 admin center

claims.claim: Admins configure visibility separately for each property.
claims.quote: Admins can configure visibility, display name, and icon for each property

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Enabled properties appear in the Contact Information section of profile cards.
claims.quote: Once enabled, properties appear in the Contact Information section of profile cards in Outlook Web

claims.quote: Once enabled, properties appear in the Contact Information section of profile cards in Outlook Web

claims.claim: The notice specifies Microsoft Graph People connectors for ingesting the properties.
claims.quote: Ingest these properties using a Microsoft Graph People connector.

claims.claim: The card feature is admin-opt-in: off by default and unchanged until an admin configures it.
claims.quote: This feature is OFF by default and requires admin configuration to enable.

claims.claim: Changes can take up to 24 hours to propagate across profile cards.
claims.quote: Changes may take up to 24 hours to propagate across profile cards.

claims.claim: The notice plans future direct ingestion from SAP SuccessFactors.
claims.quote: Future updates will include direct ingestion from SAP SuccessFactors and Workday connectors.

claims.claim: The notice plans future direct ingestion from Workday connectors.
claims.quote: Future updates will include direct ingestion from SAP SuccessFactors and Workday connectors.

claims.claim: MC1193692 was updated on 6 November 2026.
claims.quote: Updated November 6, 2026: We have updated the timeline.

claims.claim: The notice targets January 2027 for rollout to begin, previously November 2026.
claims.quote: We will begin rolling out in January 2027 (previously November 2026)

claims.claim: The notice expects rollout completion in January 2027, previously November 2026.
claims.quote: expect to complete in January 2027 (previously November 2026).

claims.claim: The notice metadata shows Microsoft's end date as 2027-03-01.
claims.quote: Published 2025-12-10; last updated 2026-11-06; Microsoft's end date 2027-03-01

claims.claim: The notice sets no act-by date.
claims.quote: Act by: none

claims.claim: Microsoft identifies tenant admins managing profile cards as the affected audience.
claims.quote: Who is affected: Microsoft 365 tenant admins managing user profile cards

claims.claim: Learn has not yet described the new connector-sourced custom-property display configuration.
claims.quote: Searched: profile cards custom properties connectors visibility API admin; Graph beta connector sourced custom profile card properties visibility icon API. Opened customize-profile-cards, peopleconnectors, build-connectors-with-people-data and add-properties-profilecard; no new display configuration.

claims.claim: Learn's profile-card page covers existing optional-property visibility settings.
claims.quote: Admins can choose to show or hide certain properties on the profile cards. They're hidden by default

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Connector people data is visible to all users in the tenant by default, rather than scoped to HR or managers.
claims.quote: By default, people data provided via a Copilot connector is visible to all users in the tenant.

claims.claim: Connector people data is stored in the user's Microsoft 365 profile.
claims.quote: This connector data is stored in the user's Microsoft 365 profile.

claims.claim: Learn documents no per-audience visibility setting for these connector-sourced custom properties.
claims.quote: Searched: people connectors profile cards custom properties audience visibility hide data deletion tenant switch. Opened peopleconnectors, customize-profile-cards, build-connectors-with-people-data and deployment-overview; people items require everyone access, with no custom-property audience setting.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The people-connector build guide requires everyone access in the ACL on ingested items.
claims.quote: You must set the access control list (ACL) on items ingested by the connector to grant access to everyone.

claims.claim: Hiding an existing optional property removes it from profile cards.
claims.quote: Hiding a property removes it from profile cards

claims.claim: Hiding an existing optional property does not delete its underlying Microsoft 365 profile data.
claims.quote: doesn't delete the underlying data from Microsoft 365 profiles

claims.claim: Hiding an existing optional property does not stop its appearance in other Microsoft 365 experiences.
claims.quote: or stop the property from appearing in other Microsoft 365 experiences.

claims.claim: The effect of hiding the new connector custom properties on other experiences and underlying data is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 connector custom profile card properties hiding underlying profile data. Opened customize-profile-cards, peopleconnectors and add-properties-profilecard; hiding guidance concerns existing optional or Entra properties, not the new custom-property control.

claims.claim: Setting up people connectors requires OAuth 2.0 authentication.
claims.quote: To set up people connectors, OAuth 2.0 authentication is required.

claims.where: Risk assessment; controls[1].note; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The people-connector page names Global Administrator and Copilot Administrator as the configuration roles.
claims.quote: Only users with Global Administrator and Copilot Administrator roles can configure people connectors.

claims.where: Risk assessment; controls[1].note; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The general connector prerequisites page instead requires AI administrator for configuration and deployment.
claims.quote: To configure and deploy Copilot connectors, you must be an AI administrator in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: People-data Copilot connectors comply with Microsoft Purview Information Barriers.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors for people data comply with information barriers (IB) to ensure compliance across various platforms.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot uses the composed connector people data.
claims.quote: Experiences such as Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft Search, profile cards, and Org Explorer use that composed people data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft Search uses the composed connector people data.
claims.quote: Experiences such as Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft Search, profile cards, and Org Explorer use that composed people data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Org Explorer uses the composed connector people data.
claims.quote: Experiences such as Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft Search, profile cards, and Org Explorer use that composed people data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Connector-ingested properties are read-only for users.
claims.quote: All properties ingested via the people connectors are read-only.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: An admin corrects connector data in the source system.
claims.quote: The administrator can update the information directly in the source system.

claims.claim: Corrected source data appears on the card after the next scheduled crawl.
claims.quote: After the connector performs its next scheduled crawl, the updated data is reflected on the user's profile card.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The included licensing model refers to the general connector requirement for tenant Microsoft 365 licenses, not a separately published custom-property entitlement.
claims.quote: Your tenant must have Microsoft 365 licenses.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Available connector types and user surfaces depend on the organisation's licensing.
claims.quote: The surfaces available to your users (Microsoft Search, Microsoft 365 Copilot grounding, Copilot Chat agents) and the connector types you can deploy depend on your organization's licensing.

claims.claim: Indexing synced connector data incurs no extra cost for tenants with Microsoft 365 licenses.
claims.quote: Indexing of synced connector data incurs no extra cost for tenants with Microsoft 365 licenses.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No licence requirement specific to the new custom profile-card properties has been published.
claims.quote: Searched: custom profile card properties licensing price meter connectors; Microsoft 365 people data connectors licensing custom profile card properties. Opened connector prerequisites, peopleconnectors, customize-profile-cards and build-connectors-with-people-data; only general licensing was documented.

claims.claim: No meter or price for the new property display is documented, including in the supplied record and notice.
claims.quote: Searched: custom profile card properties licensing price meter connectors. Read the roadmap, MC1193692, connector prerequisites, peopleconnectors and customize-profile-cards; none names a custom-property display price or meter.

claims.where: Scope: Roles; controls[0].note; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Global Administrator or People Administrator can modify People settings and the documented profile-card settings.
claims.quote: To view or modify People settings, you must be a Global Administrator or have the People Administrator role in Microsoft 365

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph ignores people-connector accounts without an Exchange Online mailbox.
claims.quote: Microsoft Graph ignores accounts without an Exchange Online mailbox.

claims.claim: Nonmatching user accounts are ignored.
claims.quote: Nonmatched user accounts (userPrincipalName or externalDirectoryObjectId) are ignored.

claims.claim: New people-data connections can take up to 6 hours to become available.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 might take up to 6 hours after the connection is created before it becomes available in search, people experiences, or Copilot.

claims.claim: People-data connections do not support staged connections.
claims.quote: Connections with people data don't support staged connections.

claims.claim: The new per-property control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > People settings > Profile > Person info on profile cards, as the notice states.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 admin center under: Settings > Org settings > People settings > Profile > Person info on profile cards

claims.claim: No API is documented for the new connector-sourced display control.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph beta connector sourced custom profile card properties visibility icon API. Opened add-properties-profilecard and Create profileCardProperty; read profileCardProperty search excerpts. These cover Entra directory attributes, not connector custom-property visibility or icons.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The people source is selected via Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Gallery > Human resources & recruiting > data source.
claims.quote: Browse the Connectors gallery in the Microsoft 365 admin center and check the Human resources & recruiting category.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections creates an external connection.
claims.quote: Create a new externalConnection object. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections

claims.claim: Existing optional properties are configured at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Services > People settings > Profile card > Contact info.
claims.quote: They're hidden by default, but admins can configure their visibility by navigating to Settings > Org settings > People settings > Profile card > Contact info in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: contentCategory is a top-level externalConnection property, not inside configuration.
claims.quote: contentCategory | microsoft.graph.externalConnectors.contentCategory | Specifies the domain category of the content associated with the external connection.

claims.claim: People-data connections must set contentCategory to people.
claims.quote: Copilot connectors that contain people data must have the value people in the contentCategory property of the externalConnections API.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/admin/people/profileCardProperties configures an Entra attribute to display on organisation profile cards.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/admin/people/profileCardProperties. The value for the Alias attribute is displayed on a user's profile card.

claims.claim: directoryPropertyName specifies the Entra directory property to display.
claims.quote: directoryPropertyName | String | The name of the directory property that is intended to surface on the profile card. Required.

claims.claim: annotations supplies alternative or localised labels.
claims.quote: annotations | profileCardAnnotation collection | Any alternative or localized labels that an administrator chose to specify. Optional.

claims.claim: isVisible controls whether the directory property is shown.
claims.quote: isVisible | Boolean | Indicates whether the given directory property should be shown on a user's profile card. Optional.

claims.claim: The existing API covers Microsoft Entra properties, including CustomAttribute1 through CustomAttribute15.
claims.quote: You can add any of the 15 Microsoft Entra ID custom extension attributes to users' profile cards

claims.claim: The profile-card API overview says delegated operations require a Tenant Administrator role.
claims.quote: Operations on the profileCardProperty resource that use delegated permissions require the signed-in user to have a Tenant Administrator role.

claims.claim: The Create profileCardProperty reference names People Administrator as the least privileged supported role.
claims.quote: People Administrator is the least privileged role supported for this operation.

claims.claim: Profile-card property writes require PeopleSettings.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | PeopleSettings.ReadWrite.All | Not available.

claims.claim: Learn recommends piloting people connectors with a limited audience.
claims.quote: Before rollout, confirm governance, privacy, and admin requirements for your connector and pilot with a limited audience.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; What's changing
claims.claim: Custom people connectors can be built with Microsoft Graph external connections APIs.
claims.quote: You build Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors for people data in the same way that you build other Copilot connectors, by using the Microsoft Graph external connections APIs.

claims.claim: The existing Entra profile-card API is not confirmed to govern connector-sourced custom properties.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph beta connector sourced custom profile card properties visibility icon API. Opened add-properties-profilecard, Create profileCardProperty and customize-profile-cards; the API's directoryPropertyName values describe Entra attributes, with no connector-property configuration.
